questions.q: As defined in the lesson, what is synthetic data?
options: Data that is artificially generated, often by another model, to stand in for real data
Data collected exclusively from social media platforms
Data that has been manually re-typed by a human from a paper form
Any dataset larger than one million rows
questions.explain: The lesson defines synthetic data as artificially generated data standing in for data collected from real people or events.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say synthetic data does not automatically solve bias concerns?
options: Synthetic data generation always removes all patterns from the source data
It still encodes the patterns of whatever real data it was modeled on, and can reproduce or amplify bias from that source
Synthetic data is always completely free of any patterns
Bias can only ever exist in data collected directly from real people
questions.explain: The lesson explains that synthetic data is typically generated from a model trained on real data, so it can inherit and even amplify that source's bias.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about synthetic data and privacy?
options: Synthetic data makes privacy risk completely impossible by definition
Synthetic data does not automatically protect privacy, and can still leak identifiable details of the real people in its source data
Synthetic data can never be generated from any real-world dataset
Privacy concerns only apply to data that is labeled by humans
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that "synthetic" is not a synonym for "anonymous" — that property has to be verified, not assumed.

questions.q: What is the one governance requirement the lesson says is genuinely new for synthetic data, compared to real data?
options: A requirement that synthetic data be deleted immediately after generation
Clear documentation that the data is synthetic, rather than blended invisibly into "the training data"
A requirement that synthetic data never be used in any model
A requirement that only government agencies may generate synthetic data
questions.explain: The lesson names documentation honesty — disclosing that data is synthetic — as the one requirement without a direct equivalent for real data.

questions.q: According to the lesson's overall framing, how should synthetic data be treated?
options: As something that should never be used under any circumstances
As a legitimate tool that still needs provenance, bias checks, and quality review — not a shortcut around governance
As data that requires no governance of any kind
As a complete replacement for all real data in every situation
questions.explain: The lesson's closing framing is that synthetic data is legitimate but still subject to the same governance questions as real data, plus the added disclosure requirement.
